beats.trigger: ## Security
beats.got: nothing new; a section header.

beats.trigger: Many frameworks exist, and each has its strengths.
beats.got: You can't judge an agent's safety from its output, so you run a check. The second paragraph is filler.

beats.trigger: The Module 4 prework adds two reads: (1) personal skills as the package format that carries expertise into your agent, (2) agent risk layered on top of normal security work.
beats.got: Homework about multi-agent coordination and skills. It is not clear why it comes before a security module.

beats.trigger: **Evaluate** residual risk: what's left after mitigation, and what future sessions need before they touch the system
beats.got: A list of six verbs. Prompt injection and residual risk are the only parts I can picture.

beats.trigger: Name the thing you'd want to check before letting this near a real stakeholder.
beats.got: Six agents are deciding things and I haven't verified any of it. That is my pricing working group's exposure.

beats.trigger: A tool call is not a new species of work. It is text crossing a boundary into action.
beats.got: A tool call is just text that the runtime turns into an action, so the risk sits at that boundary.

beats.trigger: By taking a proactive stance today, you position your organisation to capture the benefits of AI while managing its risks.
beats.got: The opening line about not being able to bet my job on it is good. Then a brochure paragraph arrives and I tune out.

beats.trigger: Your firewall doesn't see it because your firewall has never had to worry about persuasion.
beats.got: The attack is plain English inside a document the agent reads. That is relevant because my team feeds agents customer docs.

beats.trigger: Scope (give the agent less). Split (break it into two agents with different trust levels).
beats.got: Five mitigations: scope, split, filter, gate, review. I could put a gate on anything that goes to the CFO.

beats.trigger: *"Hope it doesn't happen"* is not one.
beats.got: After a mitigation you write down the residual risk and either accept it on record or close the door.

beats.trigger: Damn, this is complex stuff.
beats.got: nothing new; this repeats that certainty isn't available and you run the loop. I got that two beats ago.

beats.trigger: A **skill** packages an expertise (rules, checklists, the moves an agent runs) into something the agent can load and use.
beats.got: A skill is a reusable check the agent can load. Forty minutes, so I want to see something I can reuse.

beats.trigger: The raw run shows which rules can be checked from files and which ones need judgment, context, or a standing evidence check.
beats.got: Some policy rules can be checked mechanically and some need judgment. The raw run sorts them.

beats.trigger: The reusable check is supposed to carry what matters in your system, not generic GDPR.
beats.got: I tell it what matters for our pricing data, and the check is built around that instead of a template. This is the useful part.

beats.trigger: You'll get a lot of questions. The grill is wide on purpose: the agent probes both lenses and won't stop at one round.
beats.got: The agent writes a policy lens and an agent-risk lens, and it will ask me a lot of questions.

beats.trigger: *"You choose. Optimise for what I can't steer."*
beats.got: I answer what I know and delegate the rest, then tighten the report until I'd read it on Monday.

beats.trigger: The project skill loads in your next session in this training directory.
beats.got: The skill is saved in a folder. It only loads from this directory, which means my team can't see it.

beats.trigger: The policy files are source material. The reusable check is the expert in the room.
beats.got: nothing new; this restates that the skill is the reusable part.

beats.trigger: The goal is not a clean bill of health.
beats.got: I run the check on my module 3 system, mitigate one risk and write down the residual.

beats.trigger: Type `/` in the prompt and look for `/security-audit` in the autocomplete list.
beats.got: A check that the skill loaded.

beats.trigger: Expect the reusable check to find things you did not think about, and to leave things "I can't tell" you thought were settled.
beats.got: The packaged lens flags things I hadn't seen and leaves rows I thought were settled as 'I can't tell'. That is the contradiction-in-my-own-setup moment I wanted.

beats.trigger: Two different lenses; some risks will overlap, some will not.
beats.got: A ranked risk list from a second lens, which I question one risk at a time.

beats.trigger: Your gut is data here.
beats.got: I pick the risk that bugs me, the agent applies a fix, and the report has a residual section I accept on record.

beats.trigger: You must do the work.
beats.got: nothing new; one mitigation is what separates a prototype from production, and the beat doesn't say how.

beats.trigger: the root instructions file now tells future sessions how to behave around the risk you found.
beats.got: The session's findings are written into the instructions file, so the next session starts stricter. That still works on Monday.

beats.trigger: Give a teammate the skill, install it in their runtime, and they can call the same method without reconstructing your prompt history.
beats.got: A skill can be handed to a teammate, which is how I'd get fourteen people on one method. It still leaves open where it lives.

beats.trigger: "I can't tell" is a real answer; closing it takes evidence.
beats.got: nothing new; a recap of the module.

beats.trigger: Your call.
beats.got: Homework: one sentence per case naming the missing organisational check. The tone is a little passive-aggressive.

beats.trigger: what check was missing around the agent's output?
beats.got: Two cases to read, Mata v. Avianca and Deloitte Australia, both about checks missing around AI output.

take_homes: Don't wait for certainty on agent safety. Run the loop: assess, mitigate one thing, name the residual, decide.
A packaged check carrying my own context (pricing data, what legal cares about) found things I hadn't seen, and that is worth more than any prompt.
The attack is ordinary text inside documents the agent reads, so I need gates and scope on what it can do with them.

monday.move: Run the security check on the pilot-cohort pricing brief agent, pick one risk, add a human gate before it goes to the pricing working group, and write the residual in the report
monday.stop_condition: One mitigation applied and the residual written in the report
monday.blocker: No shared place to keep the skill and context files, so my team would each hold their own copy

misconception.why: What helped was the packaged check carrying my specific context and rules, not better prompt wording. I still think prompts matter, but they are not the main thing.

one_line: The first half is a lot of 'security is a journey' talk, but the audit exercise found things I hadn't thought of, and I now have a check I can reuse.
